constants.name: TXML_ATTR_NS_DECL
constants.doc: xmlns or xmlns:prefix

constants.name: TXML_ATTR_DEFAULTED
constants.doc: supplied by an internal-subset ATTLIST default

constants.name: TXML_NODE_EMPTY
constants.doc: written as

constants.name: TXML_NODE_CDATA
constants.doc: text written as a CDATA section; always its own node

constants.name: TXML_NODE_OPEN
constants.doc: the end tag has not been parsed yet

constants.name: TXML_WRITE_DECLARATION
constants.doc: emit < ?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>

constants.name: TXML_WRITE_INDENT
constants.doc: indent element content by depth

constants.name: TXML_WRITE_EMPTY_TAGS
constants.doc: write childless elements as

txml_allocator_free_params.doc:
======================================================================== Allocation

The embedder supplies one allocator. There is no realloc: txml never moves what it has allocated, so every pointer it hands out stays valid until the owning object is destroyed.

fields.name: alloc
fields.doc: Return `size` bytes aligned to `alignment`, or NULL.

fields.name: free
fields.doc: Release a block obtained from alloc(); `params` repeats its size and alignment, so the embedder needs no header of its own.

fields.name: head
fields.doc: newest chunk; each chunk links to the previous

fields.name: chunk_size
fields.doc: minimum payload size of the next chunk

fields.name: used
fields.doc: bytes handed out to callers

fields.name: reserved
fields.doc: bytes obtained from the backing allocator

txml_arena_chunk.doc:
======================================================================== Arena

A bump allocator over a linked list of chunks. Growing links a new chunk in front of the old ones; nothing is copied and no address changes. A document owns two of these (ADR 0016) and neither ever relocates, which is why every txml_str a document hands out is valid for that document's lifetime.

A request larger than the chunk size gets a chunk of its own, so a single allocation is always contiguous.

constants.name: TXML_ARENA_VALUES
constants.doc: the byte pool, and the name and namespace columns

constants.name: TXML_ARENA_TREE
constants.doc: the node, attribute, and position columns

txml_arena_kind.doc: A document owns two arenas, split by lifetime (ADR 0016): values are written once and live as long as the document, the tree is appended as it parses. Both are destroyed by txml_doc_destroy. `limits.max_document_bytes` bounds the sum of their `used`.

txml_arena_mark.doc: A position in an arena, for releasing everything allocated after it.

fields.name: prefix
fields.doc: The prefix this attribute was written with, empty when there was none. Not part of the name's identity: `p:k` and `q:k` in one namespace are one name ID with two prefixes. A namespace declaration reports "xmlns" (or empty for a default declaration); a defaulted attribute reports the prefix its ATTLIST default was written with.

txml_cursor.doc:
======================================================================== Cursors

A cursor is a value: a document and a node index. Copy it, store it, compare indices for document order. It owns nothing and allocates nothing.

Cursor calls are total: they never allocate and never return an API error. A cursor whose index is out of range, or that was made for another document, reads as absent — TXML_NONE, TXML_NAME_NONE, TXML_INDEX_NONE, an empty txml_str, false, and TXML_NODE_DOCUMENT from txml_kind, which has no absent value of its own. Mixing cursors from two documents is still a bug; it is simply not one the library can report.

txml_document_error.doc: A well-formedness failure. `message` is a fixed English phrase owned by the library and valid for the process lifetime; it is a diagnostic, not an API contract. Document errors are data: they never arrive as a txml_result from a cursor call.

constants.name: TXML_DOC_ENCODING
constants.doc: not well-formed UTF-8, or a forbidden character

constants.name: TXML_DOC_SYNTAX
constants.doc: malformed markup

constants.name: TXML_DOC_NAME
constants.doc: not a legal XML name

constants.name: TXML_DOC_TAG_MISMATCH
constants.doc: end tag does not match the open element

constants.name: TXML_DOC_UNEXPECTED_EOF
constants.doc: input ended inside markup or with elements open

constants.name: TXML_DOC_NO_ROOT
constants.doc: no document element

constants.name: TXML_DOC_TRAILING_CONTENT
constants.doc: content after the document element

constants.name: TXML_DOC_LIMIT
constants.doc: a txml_limits value was reached; see `limit`

txml_find.doc: A name scan over a node range: the fastest query the document supports.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: the name ID to match

fields.name: bound
fields.doc: stop before this index; TXML_INDEX_NONE means the whole document

txml_limit_kind.doc: Which limit a TXML_DOC_LIMIT error reached.

txml_limits.doc: Two limits have representation ceilings, because a node's depth is stored as uint16_t and pool offsets are uint32_t: max_depth may not exceed 65535 and max_document_bytes may not exceed UINT32_MAX. A configuration that exceeds either is rejected by txml_parser_init() with TXML_ERR_INVALID.

fields.name: max_depth
fields.doc: element nesting; at most 65535

fields.name: max_attributes
fields.doc: attributes on one element

fields.name: max_name_length
fields.doc: bytes in one qualified name

fields.name: max_names
fields.doc: distinct expanded names per document

fields.name: max_document_bytes
fields.doc: values + tree arena bytes; at most UINT32_MAX

fields.name: entity_expansion_budget
fields.doc: bytes produced by entity expansion

constants.name: TXML_MOVED
constants.doc: the cursor now points at the requested node

constants.name: TXML_NONE
constants.doc: there is no such node; the cursor did not move

constants.name: TXML_PENDING
constants.doc: the answer needs input not parsed yet; the cursor did not move

constants.name: TXML_NODE_DOCUMENT
constants.doc: index 0; the parent of everything else

constants.name: TXML_NODE_DECLARATION
constants.doc: < ?xml ...?>; its pseudo-attributes are attributes

constants.name: TXML_NODE_DOCTYPE
constants.doc: < !DOCTYPE ...>; its text is the declaration as written

txml_parser.doc:
======================================================================== Parser

The parser is fed byte chunks and produces a concrete syntax tree: comments, processing instructions, whitespace, the XML declaration and the DOCTYPE are all nodes, so a parsed document writes back as what it was. It never reads from a file, socket, or entity resolver: external entities and external DTDs are not fetched, which removes XXE by construction.

fields.name: allocator
fields.doc: The document creates both of its arenas over this allocator and destroys them with itself; the caller supplies no arena of its own.

fields.name: staging_length
fields.doc: input window in bytes; sizes a chunk, not a construct; 0 selects 64 KiB

fields.name: chunk_size
fields.doc: chunk size for both arenas; 0 selects TXML_ARENA_CHUNK_DEFAULT

fields.name: step_budget
fields.doc: nodes appended per step; 0 means until the step blocks

txml_position.doc: A location in the input. `offset` counts bytes from the first byte fed to the parser; `line` and `column` count from 1, and `column` counts bytes.

txml_qname.doc: An expanded name: the namespace URI (empty when there is none) and the local part. Prefixes are not part of a name's identity.

constants.name: TXML_OK
constants.doc: The call succeeded.

constants.name: TXML_NEED_SPACE
constants.doc: Writer only: the output buffer is full. Drain it and continue.

constants.name: TXML_ERR_INVALID
constants.doc: API misuse: a null handle, a cursor from another document, a call in the wrong order. Never caused by document content.

constants.name: TXML_ERR_NOMEM
constants.doc: The backing allocator refused a request.

constants.name: TXML_ERR_LIMIT
constants.doc: A txml_limits value was reached.

constants.name: TXML_ERR_NOT_FOUND
constants.doc: The requested name, attribute, or node does not exist.

constants.name: TXML_ERR_PENDING
constants.doc: The answer depends on input that has not been parsed yet.

constants.name: TXML_ERR_DOCUMENT
constants.doc: The document is not well-formed; read txml_parser_error() for details.

constants.name: TXML_STEP_PROGRESS
constants.doc: the step budget was used up; call again

constants.name: TXML_STEP_NEED_INPUT
constants.doc: feed more bytes, or feed final = true

constants.name: TXML_STEP_NEED_MEMORY
constants.doc: the allocator refused; give it more and call again

constants.name: TXML_STEP_DONE
constants.doc: the document is complete

constants.name: TXML_STEP_FAILED
constants.doc: not well-formed; read txml_parser_error()

txml_str.doc: Text and bytes. Both are borrowed views: the `ptr`/`length` pair never owns its storage. Lengths are byte counts, never character counts.

txml_write_name.doc: A name to write. An empty `prefix` with a non-empty `ns` asks the writer to pick or reuse a prefix; an empty `ns` writes an unqualified name.

txml_writer.doc:
======================================================================== Writer

The writer takes events and fills a caller buffer. It knows nothing about documents: anything that can emit start/attribute/text/end can produce XML. txml_write_subtree() is the bridge from a parsed document.

fields.name: allocator
fields.doc: backs the writer's element and namespace stack

fields.name: output
fields.doc: filled by the writer, drained by the caller

functions.name: txml_arena_alloc
functions.doc: Allocate `size` bytes aligned to `alignment` (a power of two). Returns NULL only when the backing allocator refuses.

functions.name: txml_arena_release
functions.doc: Free every chunk newer than `mark` and resume bump allocation there. One spare chunk is retained to avoid churn.

functions.name: txml_arena_reset
functions.doc: Free every chunk but keep the arena usable.

functions.name: txml_parse_feed
functions.doc:
Copy up to `chunk.length` bytes into the parser's staging window and return how many were taken. The caller may reuse or free the chunk as soon as the call returns. Pass `final = true` only with the chunk that ends the document; if fewer bytes than offered are accepted, the flag is ignored and the caller repeats it with the rest. A caller that ignores the return value silently truncates its document, which surfaces as TXML_DOC_UNEXPECTED_EOF. Feeding after final is TXML_ERR_INVALID reported by the next step.

An XML declaration becomes a TXML_NODE_DECLARATION whose version, encoding and standalone pseudo-attributes are ordinary attributes, so it is read with txml_first_attribute and txml_find_attribute like any element. A declaration naming an encoding other than UTF-8 is TXML_DOC_ENCODING. What the writer emits is governed by TXML_WRITE_DECLARATION alone.

functions.name: txml_parse_step
functions.doc: Parse staged input. Each call appends nodes until the step budget is used up or the parser blocks.

functions.name: txml_parser_doc
functions.doc: The document under construction. Valid from init until the parser is destroyed or the document is detached; readable while parsing.

functions.name: txml_parser_error
functions.doc: The failure that ended the parse. TXML_ERR_NOT_FOUND while none happened.

functions.name: txml_parser_offset
functions.doc: Bytes accepted by txml_parse_feed() so far.

functions.name: txml_parser_finish
functions.doc: Detach the finished document and destroy the parser. Only after TXML_STEP_DONE; otherwise TXML_ERR_INVALID and nothing is destroyed.

functions.name: txml_parser_destroy
functions.doc: Destroy the parser and, unless it was detached, its document.

functions.name: txml_doc_destroy
functions.doc: Destroy a detached document and both of its arenas.

functions.name: txml_doc_find_name
functions.doc: Resolve an expanded name to this document's name ID, or TXML_NAME_NONE when the document does not contain it. A query that resolves to TXML_NAME_NONE can be answered without scanning anything.

functions.name: txml_doc_node_count
functions.doc: Nodes appended so far, including the document node.

functions.name: txml_doc_arena
functions.doc: Accounting for one of the document's arenas.

functions.name: txml_doc_root
functions.doc: Navigation. Every function moves the cursor only on TXML_MOVED.

functions.name: txml_next_element
functions.doc: The next sibling that is an element, skipping text, comments, and PIs.

functions.name: txml_index
functions.doc: Ranges. A subtree is [txml_index(c), txml_subtree_end(c)).

functions.name: txml_subtree_end
functions.doc: One past the last descendant, or TXML_INDEX_NONE while the node is open.

functions.name: txml_contains
functions.doc: Whether `node` is `ancestor` itself or one of its descendants. False while `ancestor` is still open.

functions.name: txml_find_next
functions.doc: Move to the next element after the cursor, below `bound`, whose name matches. TXML_NONE when there is none.

functions.name: txml_kind
functions.doc: Reading.

functions.name: txml_node_name_id
functions.doc: The element's or PI target's name ID; TXML_NAME_NONE for other kinds.

functions.name: txml_node_prefix
functions.doc: The prefix as written, empty when there was none. Not part of identity.

functions.name: txml_node_text
functions.doc: Text of a TEXT, COMMENT, PI, or DOCTYPE node, normalized; empty for other kinds. A DECLARATION carries its parts as attributes, not as text.

functions.name: txml_node_position
functions.doc: Every node has a position; TXML_ERR_INVALID only for an absent cursor.

functions.name: txml_attribute_count
functions.doc: Attributes, in document order.

functions.name: txml_find_attribute
functions.doc: Look up one attribute by name ID. An unprefixed attribute has no namespace, so a default xmlns does not apply to it.

functions.name: txml_write_start
functions.doc: Every emit call returns TXML_OK or TXML_NEED_SPACE. On TXML_NEED_SPACE the caller writes out txml_writer_output() and calls txml_writer_drain(), which continues the interrupted call and may return TXML_NEED_SPACE again. Text passed to a call that returned TXML_NEED_SPACE must stay valid until that call finally returns TXML_OK.

functions.name: txml_write_pi
functions.doc: A processing instruction: ` < ?target data?>`. The target is an unqualified name; the data is written verbatim and may not contain "?>".

functions.name: txml_write_subtree
functions.doc: Write a node and its descendants. Resumable: the writer remembers where in the walk it stopped, and drains continue it.

functions.name: txml_writer_output
functions.doc: Bytes produced and not yet consumed.

functions.name: txml_writer_drain
functions.doc: Consume them and continue any interrupted operation.

functions.name: txml_writer_finish
functions.doc: Check that every element was closed. Remaining bytes stay in the output.

functions.name: txml_str_equal
functions.doc:
======================================================================== Text helpers

txml uses no C library, so these are the comparisons it needs internally and callers usually want too.

functions.name: txml_str_starts_with
functions.doc: Whether `text` begins with `prefix`; the SCXML event-descriptor case.
